lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.17 - A Listen and read.

details: Listen and read develops students’ ability to connect spoken language with written text. It helps them build confidence in reading along with audio support.
Look for careful listening, accurate recognition of key vocabulary, and appropriate intonation when reading aloud.

“There are lots of things we need to do for the party. But what do we do first? I need some ideas… let’s listen to what these children did! Switch on your listening ears! Listen carefully and follow closely with your fingers to check. Don’t forget to switch your ears off when you’re done!”

Heads Up (Reading): 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and help Ss to understand the text by asking questions, practicing skimming (reading for gist), scanning (reading for specific information) and detail (reading for comprehension). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down (Listen and Follow): 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together (Video, then act it out): 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.17 - B. Choose or write the correct answers.

details: Choose or write checks students’ understanding of the text, reinforcing comprehension and writing skills. Writing reinforces whole-word memory, letter order, and neat handwriting.
Look for appropriate answers that show the student understands the text and context given, as well as spelling and writing accuracy.
“Oh dear! Emma, Brian and Tony need our help. Let’s help them solve the questions together.”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

Project Gallery:

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.73 - A Read and correct.

details: Read and correct helps students check their understanding of sentences by finding mistakes and fixing them. It strengthens reading accuracy, sentence meaning, and careful attention to detail.
Look for correct identification of errors in the sentences, logical corrections and clear handwriting.
“Oh no! A mini monster snuck into our party and mixed up the sentences. Let’s read them carefully so we can fix his silly mistakes before he causes more trouble!”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.73 - B Read and circle T (True) or F (False)

details: Read and circle T (True) or F (False) checks students’ understanding of the text and builds comprehension, careful reading, and pupils’ confidence in making simple decisions.
Look for accurate answers based on the text, a correct understanding of the story and the sentences, and clear circling of T or F.
“These sentences have hidden secrets, and only real detectives can find them! Read each sentence and decide if it’s true or false.”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.73 - C Match and write

details: Match and write lets students match up split words and practise writing them. It supports vocabulary recall, matching, and correct spelling.
Look for correct answers, accurate spelling, neat and clear handwriting.
“That cheeky monster split our words in two. Can you figure out which two should go together? Write them down carefully and we can beat him.”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.18 - C Imagine your class is having a party. Write and share.

details: Write and share helps students express simple ideas in writing and communicate them to others. It reinforces sentence building and builds confidence.
Look for simple, clear sentences about the party, correct use of target vocabulary, and neat handwriting.
“Exciting news! We’re going to have a big party! Write down your ideas so we can make the party amazing, then share them with your friends so everyone knows the plan.”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.18 - D Make your own conversation.

details: Make your own conversation gives students the chance to use the target language in a short dialogue. It strengthens oral fluency.
Look for clear, simple exchanges, natural turn-taking, correct question and answer patterns, and confident speaking.
“I love Pass the Parcel! What’s your favourite party game? Share your ideas with a partner and then choose the best one between you.”
